body.p:
Pushing and pulling are some of the most common git workflows. If you are unfamiliar with them, see the Git documentation:
Git Push Documentation
Git Pull Documentation
The Git Client supports the following push and pull actions:

ul.li: Use to make changes available in the remote repository after you commit them to a local repository.

Use Pull to bring other people's commits from the remote repository into your local repository.
In the Pull drop-down menu, you can choose between Pull (merge) and Pull (rebase). The action you choose becomes the default action of the toolbar button.
Use Pull... when you need to pull from a remote branch other than the tracked branch.

body.note: When you push a local branch that does not have a corresponding remote branch, a remote branch with the same name is created automatically.

section.title: Push changes
section.p: Push changes to integrate commits from a local branch into its remote upstream.
Before you push, pull changes to ensure your local branch is up-to-date with its remote upstream.
To push changes, follow these steps:

ol.li:
If your branch is behind the remote branch, the Git Client will not let you push and raises an error:
Pushing changes while behind raises an error

If file conflicts appear, resolve them.

section.p: Pull commits to bring your local branch up to date with its remote upstream.
